17.11.2023 Order No.

Since both the BLAPLs relate to the same P.S. Case (Cyber Crime and Economic Offences,
UPD, Cuttack P.S. Case No.08 of 2023), on the consent of the learned counsel for the Petitioners as well as State, they are taken up together and are disposed of by this common order.

2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners and learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State.
3.

The Petitioners are accused in connection with G.R. Case No.221 of 2023, pending on the file of the learned J.M.F.C.-I, (Cog. Taking), Cuttack, arising out of Cyber Crime and Economic Offences,
UPD, Cuttack P.S. Case No.08 of 2023 for alleged commission of offences under Sections 419/420/384/467/468/471/201/120-B/34 of IPC read with Section 66-D/67/67-A/84-C of I.T. Act.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the rejection of their application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Cuttack, by orders dated 07.09.2023 and 04.09.2023 respectively in the aforementioned cases, the present BLAPLs have been filed.

5. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner (Bighneswar Parimanik) in BLAPL No.10521 of 2023 is in custody since 27.04.2023 and the Petitioner (Sakir Khan) in BLAPL No.10327 of 2023 is in custody since 22.04.2023.

6. The allegation against the present Petitioners is that they are part of the extortion racket for which the informant was forced to part with sum of about Rs.8,00,000/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs).
7.
It is apt to state here that this is the second journey of the Petitioners to this Court.
Earlier by order dated 16.08.2023 this Court did not grant bail to the Petitioners since the investigation was continuing.

8. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioners that since admittedly, charge sheet has already been filed on 17.08.2023 and taking into account the nature of allegation, the role ascribed to them, further continuance of the Petitioners in custody is not warranted.

9. Affidavits at the behest of the Petitioners filed indicating that the Petitioner (Bighneswar Parimanik) in BLAPL No.10521 of 2023 is the first offender and the Petitioner (Sakir Khan) in BLAPL No.10327 of 2023 has one criminal antecedent of the year 2015 but not of similar nature.
10. Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail and submits that further investigation is continuing and taking into account the nature thereof and as the Petitioner (Sakir Khan) in BLAPL No.10327 of 2023 is also a flight risk, the bail applications of the present Petitioners ought not to be considered at this stage.

11. Taking into account the nature of allegations, role ascribed to the Petitioners, punishment prescribed, the progress in investigation and period of custody, this Court directs the Petitioners to be released on bail on such terms to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin.
12. Before releasing, learned Court in seisin is requested to verify assertions regarding the criminal antecedent of the Petitioners, as noted above.
If it comes to fore that such assertions regarding the criminal antecedent of the Petitioners is incorrect, this order shall not be given effect to.

13. Additionally, it is directed that the Petitioner (Bighneswar Parimanik) in BLAPL No.10521 of 2023 shall furnish unencumbered property security to the tune of Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs) to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin and the Petitioner (Sakir Khan) in BLAPL No.10327 of 2023 in addition to the local surety shall furnish unencumbered property security to the same amount and the property surety shall abide by the final result of the trial.

14. It is further directed that the Petitioners shall appear before the jurisdictional police station once every month on such date and time to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin till conclusion of trial.

16. Accordingly, both the BLAPLs stand disposed of.
